reports.lens: manifest — manifest and resume semantics (workspace.read_manifest / write_manifest_row / build_workspace done flags, dock._save)

findings.title: Any OSError/ValueError from write_manifest_row inside _save aborts the whole app (SIGABRT) after the export files were already written
findings.description: export_item is wrapped in try/except, but the following write_manifest_row(...) call is not. Any failure there propagates out of the Qt slot and PyQt5 calls qFatal. Reproduced three ways through the real Save button: (a) <out>/manifest.csv is a directory -> IsADirectoryError at os.replace; (b) out dir chmod 500 after png/ already exists -> PermissionError creating manifest.csv.tmp; (c) manifest.csv carries an extra column (e.g. a 'note' column added in a spreadsheet) -> ValueError 'dict contains fields not in fieldnames' from csv.DictWriter (workspace.py:244). In every case the product files were already (over)written on disk when the process died, the item is not marked done and manifest.csv.tmp is left behind. In case (b) png/a_mask.png on disk now holds the 2nd stroke (3248 px) while the manifest still records the 1st (2124 px). Ctrl+S / Save & Next go through the same slot.

findings.observed: rc=134, stderr traceback ending in IsADirectoryError / PermissionError / ValueError raised from workspace.write_manifest_row via annotation_dock._save; 'ALIVE after save' never printed; out dir holds png/a_mask.png + manifest.csv.tmp; item.done stays False.
findings.expected: An 'Export failed'-style dialog (as for export_item errors) and the app keeps running with the item left pending; no stray .tmp.

findings.title: Unparseable manifest (non-UTF-8 byte or NUL-filled tail) aborts the app on Open directory
findings.description: read_manifest only catches OSError and KeyError. A latin-1 byte in a path raises UnicodeDecodeError, and a NUL-filled tail (classic crash/zero-fill artefact) raises _csv.Error 'line contains NUL'. build_workspace (workspace.py:191) is called inside the _open_dir slot (annotation_dock.py:284), so the exception kills the process before any workspace is shown. The same read happens inside write_manifest_row on every Save.
findings.repro_cmd: cd /tmp && QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen timeout 300 ~/miniconda3/envs/viewer_vidi/bin/python /tmp/claude-1000/-home-zsk/714d8704-0f43-42f9-ba79-d4ec2a9ad51f/scratchpad/stab/manifest/repro_abort_manifest_write.py nonutf8   # also: nul
findings.observed: rc=134 right after clicking Open directory; stderr: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe4 ... / _csv.Error: line contains NUL, raised from workspace.read_manifest via build_workspace via annotation_dock._open_dir.
findings.expected: Workspace opens with a warning that the manifest could not be read (all items pending), or the manifest is read with errors='replace'; never a process abort.

findings.title: Manifest with a UTF-8 BOM (Excel 'CSV UTF-8') or a missing header line is read as empty, and the next Save silently rewrites it with a single row
findings.description: With a BOM the first header becomes '﻿stem', so r.get('stem') is None for every row and read_manifest returns {}. A manifest whose header line was deleted behaves the same. build_workspace then marks all items pending (the GUI shows '0 done'), and because write_manifest_row does read-modify-write on that empty dict, the first Save replaces the whole file with just the new row — every previous row (source path, rect, mask count, files) is gone, with no dialog. Reproduced in the GUI (bom_manifest scenario: done=[False,False,False], manifest after one save = ['a'] instead of ['a','b','c']) and in pure Python.
findings.observed: bom: read_manifest -> [] (expected ['a','b']); after saving 'c' -> ['c']; file contents: header + the c row only. nohdr: identical.
findings.expected: Open with encoding='utf-8-sig' so a BOM is tolerated; and refuse to overwrite (or back up) a manifest file that exists but yielded zero rows.

findings.title: Duplicate basenames: adding or removing one file re-keys the stems, so a never-annotated file resumes as done and the annotated one reverts to pending
findings.description: unique_stems gives a file the plain basename stem unless ANOTHER file with the same basename exists. The manifest is keyed by stem only, so the done flag follows the stem, not the file. Workspace a.png + sub/a.png -> stems 'a' / 'sub__a'. Annotate only a.png (row 'a'). Delete a.png: sub/a.png now gets stem 'a' and resumes as done=True (it was never annotated; a Save would overwrite a.png's outputs under the same names). Re-add a.png: the fresh a.png shows done while sub/a.png is pending. Same mechanism for a.png vs a.PNG ('a' / 'a_1').
findings.observed: deleted a.png -> sub/a.png: stem 'a' done=True; re-added a.png (never annotated) -> a.png stem 'a' done=True, sub/a.png stem 'sub__a' done=False.
findings.expected: Done flags should be matched to the file (e.g. by the 'source' column or a path-derived stem), so items only show done when that file was saved.

findings.title: Outputs of a previous Output dir name (or Output dir '.') are rescanned as job items on reopen
findings.description: scan_images skips only the directory named by the CURRENT out_dir_name. After saving item a into vidi_output and item b into out2 (Output dir edited mid-job, which _save honours via ws.out_dir_name at annotation_dock.py:423), reopening the directory with 'out2' lists stems ['a','b','c','a_mask'] (vidi_output/png/a_mask.png became an item); reopening with 'vidi_output' lists ['a','b','c','b_mask']. With Output dir '.', png/ lands in the workspace root and png/a_mask.png becomes an item of its own on reopen. Done flags on reopen come solely from the currently named dir's manifest (a or b, never both) — consistent with the code but the in-session list had shown both as done ('2 done').
findings.observed: saved with 'vidi_output', reopened with 'out2': items = ['a.png', 'vidi_output/png/a_mask.png']; saved/reopened with '.': items = ['a.png', 'png/a_mask.png'].
findings.expected: Exported mask/roi/image files never appear as job items (skip any dir holding a manifest.csv, or reject '.'/'..'-style output names).

findings.title: Concurrent saves from two instances share one manifest.csv.tmp: FileNotFoundError (abort in the GUI) and rows dropped
findings.description: write_manifest_row writes to the fixed name <manifest>.csv.tmp and os.replace()s it. Two processes saving at the same instant race: one replace removes the other's tmp -> FileNotFoundError (in the GUI this is the unhandled-slot abort of finding 1), and the read-modify-write cycle loses rows. Sequential alternation between two instances (A,B,A,B... 20 rows) was fine: all rows present, last writer wins without loss. Only reproduced by hammering from 3 pure-Python processes, not in the GUI, hence low confidence that it matters in practice.
findings.observed: exit codes [0, 1, 1]; FileNotFoundError: ... manifest.csv.tmp -> manifest.csv; rows kept: 50 / 150.
findings.expected: 150 rows and no error (unique tmp name per writer, e.g. tempfile in the same dir, plus a lock or append-only log).

findings.title: Re-saving an item with other formats or without the rectangle leaves stale outputs on disk that the manifest no longer lists
findings.description: export_item never removes earlier products of the same stem. Save #1 (png, mask+rect) writes a_mask/a_roi/a_roi_mask.png; save #2 (nifti) adds the nifti set and the manifest 'files' now lists only nifti/...; save #3 (png, new mask, rect dropped) rewrites a_mask.png but png/a_roi.png + png/a_roi_mask.png from save #1 (old rectangle, old mask: 1543 px vs 1249 px expected from the new mask) stay beside it. A consumer that globs png/ gets an inconsistent set; only the manifest row is correct. Reproduced in the GUI (stale_files) and pure Python.
findings.observed: after save3: manifest files='png/a_mask.png'; disk: nifti/a_mask.nii.gz nifti/a_roi.nii.gz nifti/a_roi_mask.nii.gz png/a_mask.png png/a_roi.png png/a_roi_mask.png.
findings.expected: Re-saving a stem removes (or at least warns about) that stem's previous products that are not part of the new set, or the manifest records them as stale.

findings.title: 'files' column is space-joined, so stems containing a space cannot be split back into paths
findings.description: files=' '.join(written). For the item 'space stem' the column reads 'png/space stem_mask.png png/space stem_roi.png png/space stem_roi_mask.png' — 3 files, 6 tokens on split. The csv quoting itself round-trips commas, quotes, umlauts, CJK and even a newline in stems correctly; only this inner separator is ambiguous.
findings.observed: files split(): ['png/space', 'stem_mask.png', 'png/space', 'stem_roi.png', 'png/space', 'stem_roi_mask.png']; GUI unicode_stems check 'every token of files exists on disk' fails only for the space stem.
findings.expected: A separator that cannot occur in paths (e.g. ';' or JSON list), or one row per file.

reports.notes: Coverage (32 pure-Python checks in t_pure.py, 44 GUI checks + 2 observed aborts across 14 isolated scenarios in t_gui.py/run_gui.py, 10 repro confirmations; all Qt runs offscreen under timeout 300, stderr captured). PASSED / benign: truncated last line (rows kept, write ok); older schema without 'files' (read ok, write upgrades with files=''); empty file and header-only (read {} , write ok); leftover manifest.csv.tmp from a crash (ignored on open, consumed on save) and a .tmp that is a directory (write raises -> same abort class as finding 1); unicode / comma / quote / space / newline stems round-trip exactly through csv quoting and resume 5/5 done in the GUI; rect-less save -> x0..y1 = '' with mask_pixels = painted count and files=png/<stem>_mask.png; mask-less (rect-only) save -> mask_pixels '0', int rect, files=png/<stem>_roi.png; Original-only save -> mask_pixels '0', empty rect, files=png/<stem>_image.png; read_manifest round-trips all three. Performance: write_manifest_row on a 5000-row manifest = 30 ms (read 12 ms, 0.76 MB); on a real 20000-row manifest = 119 ms (linear, so ~120 ms at 20k as estimated); GUI Save click with 5000 rows = 33 ms, open 217 ms. Read-only out dir BEFORE any subdir exists -> export_item raises, 'Export failed' QMessageBox shown, process survives, item stays pending, mask kept, and the save succeeds after chmod back (good path; the abort only happens once png/ exists and the manifest write is what fails). Saving an item, deleting its source, reopening -> item disappears from the list, manifest keeps its row, next pending loads, no crash; deleting the displayed item's source then Save -> succeeds from in-memory pixels and records the vanished path (noted, not reported). Two instances saving alternately (20 sequential writes) -> all rows present, no loss; loss/crash only under true concurrency (finding 6). Changing Output dir mid-job: Save honours the new name, in-session list shows done flags from both dirs ('2 done') while reopen shows only the named dir's manifest — consistent with the code, reported only for the item-list leak (finding 5). Saving the same item twice keeps one manifest row and '1 done' (no double count). Documented limitations (2-D, one item per file, done item not reloading its mask) were not reported. All findings are in the new untracked files (workspace.py, annotation_dock.py, annotation_export.py) so preexisting=false throughout. Scratch dirs chmod'ed back to writable after the tests.

reports.lens: listparse — workspace.py parse_list_file / find_list_files / build_workspace / unique_stems and the dock's Open list… / Open directory… flows

findings.title: NUL byte in a .csv/.tsv list (e.g. UTF-16 CSV) raises _csv.Error and aborts the app from Open list… AND Open directory…
findings.description: parse_list_file feeds every non-blank line of a .csv/.tsv to csv.reader without catching csv.Error. On the env's Python 3.10 any NUL byte raises `_csv.Error: line contains NUL`. The exception escapes the dock's _open_list slot (annotation_dock.py:309). Worse, find_list_files (workspace.py:168) parses every .csv/.tsv directly in a root, and probe_workspace calls it on every Open directory…, so an image folder that merely contains a UTF-16-encoded CSV (LibreOffice/Excel 'Unicode' export) kills the viewer even in image mode. PyQt5 turns the unhandled slot exception into qFatal: exit 134, core dumped.

findings.observed: `_csv.Error: line contains NUL` at workspace.py:124 from annotation_dock._open_list (and from find_list_files via _open_dir); process exits 134 (SIGABRT). Same for lists/nul.tsv (one NUL inside a label cell).
findings.expected: parse_list_file returns [] / skips the bad line (or decodes with errors handled) and the dock shows the 'Empty list' / 'Empty workspace' message; no exception in a Qt slot.

findings.title: A .csv/.tsv field longer than 131072 chars raises _csv.Error 'field larger than field limit' and aborts the app
findings.description: csv.field_size_limit() defaults to 131072; a list CSV with a long free-text/blob column (or random binary bytes named .csv, as in lists/binary.csv) raises `_csv.Error: field larger than field limit (131072)`. Uncaught, it escapes _open_list (annotation_dock.py:309) and find_list_files (workspace.py:168, reached by every Open directory…), so the process aborts with exit 134.

findings.observed: `_csv.Error: field larger than field limit (131072)` at workspace.py:124; exit 134, core dumped. Also reproduced with lists/longfield.tsv and lists/binary.csv (200 kB random bytes).
findings.expected: The oversized row is skipped or the path column is still read; no abort.

findings.title: A .txt list line starting with '~' that contains a NUL byte raises ValueError in os.path.expanduser and aborts the app
findings.description: _resolve calls os.path.expanduser on every entry. For '~name…' posixpath.expanduser calls pwd.getpwnam(name), which raises `ValueError: embedded null byte` when the name contains NUL. A 2 MB random-byte file named binary.txt hit this on its line 369. Because find_list_files parses every .txt in a root, a stray binary file with a .txt extension in an image folder makes Open directory… abort as well. Exit 134.
findings.repro_cmd: cd /tmp && QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen timeout 300 ~/miniconda3/envs/viewer_vidi/bin/python /tmp/claude-1000/-home-zsk/714d8704-0f43-42f9-ba79-d4ec2a9ad51f/scratchpad/stab/listparse/repro/repro_tilde_nul.py   # list.txt with line '~user\x00name/a.dcm'; 'pure' for module-only
findings.observed: `ValueError: embedded null byte` from posixpath.expanduser ← workspace._resolve (line 152) ← parse_list_file ← annotation_dock._open_list; exit 134. Same traceback with lists/binary.txt.
findings.expected: Entries that cannot be resolved are skipped or counted as missing; no exception.

findings.title: UTF-8 BOM in a .txt list sticks to the first path, which is then reported 'not found' with a visually identical tooltip path
findings.description: The list is opened with encoding='utf-8' (not 'utf-8-sig'), so '﻿' stays on line 1. _resolve sees '﻿/abs/a.dcm' as a relative path and joins it to the list directory, producing '<listdir>/﻿/abs/a.dcm', which does not exist. Windows Notepad and Excel 'CSV UTF-8' write this BOM by default. The dock shows '1 items … 1 listed path(s) not found' and the tooltip shows a path that looks exactly like the real file (the BOM is invisible), so the user cannot tell why the first image is missing. CSV/TSV variants happen to survive because the unknown-header heuristic drops the BOM'd header row.
findings.observed: parsed[0] = '<listdir>/﻿/<abs>/a.dcm'; ws.items = ['b'], ws.missing = [that path]. In the dock: label '… 1 items, 0 done · 1 listed path(s) not found', tooltip contains U+FEFF.
findings.expected: Both entries resolve; items = ['a','b'], nothing missing.

findings.title: Header-less CSV: a missing extensionless path in row 1 is silently swallowed as a 'header' (not an item, not in ws.missing)
findings.description: When no known header name is found, parse_list_file drops the first row if its first cell has no '.' in its basename AND does not exist on disk. For extensionless DICOM paths (CD/scanner exports like …/54450002/42228791) that rule is exactly 'the first listed file is missing', so the row disappears from both the items and the missing count — the user sees 'N items, 0 not found' and never learns that a listed file is gone. The same rule drops the first data row of an id-first CSV ('1,x,/abs/a.dcm') so that case ends in 'Empty list' instead of 2 missing entries; the README documents only 'else the first column', not this heuristic.
findings.observed: cohort.csv = '<dir>/42228791,x' (deleted) + '<dir>/42228802,y' (exists) → parsed = [42228802 only]; items 1, missing [] (expected missing = [42228791]).
findings.expected: Row 1 is either an item or reported under 'listed path(s) not found'; the missing count should be 1.

findings.title: Duplicate basenames outside the workspace root get the whole absolute path as stem; deep paths exceed 255 chars so the item can never be saved
findings.description: unique_stems falls back to relpath(root); when the entry lies outside the root (the normal case for list mode, where entries are absolute paths into a data archive) it uses the full absolute path with '/' → '__'. Colliding DICOM basenames (IM0001.dcm, 1.dcm …) across series are common. With directories ~240 chars deep the stem is 329 chars; every export then fails with `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long` (the dock shows 'Export failed', the item stays pending forever). Even in ordinary cases the stems are ~110-char strings like 'tmp__claude-1000__-home-zsk__…__imgs__sub__a' (observed with lists/dotdot.txt), which is what the user sees in the job list and in the output file names.
findings.observed: stem lengths [329, 329]; export_item → PIL Image.save → OSError Errno 36 File name too long '…/png/tmp__claude-1000__…__a_mask.png'.
findings.expected: Stems stay within filesystem limits (e.g. a short parent-folder prefix or numeric suffix), so every listed item can be saved.

findings.title: List mode accepts any existing file as an item; an item the viewer cannot open blocks Prev/Next/Save&Next and, if first, disables navigation entirely
findings.description: build_workspace (workspace.py:186) keeps every path that is a file, with no image check (image mode filters with is_image_path). A DICOM named x.ima/y.dicom, a PNG without extension, the list file itself (lists/self.txt → item 'self') or a README's 'LICENSE.txt' all become items. _load_index sets the 'Cannot open …' status and returns before updating _index, and _step just calls _load_index(_index+delta), so Next/Prev retry the same unloadable item forever; the only escape is double-clicking a later item. When the FIRST item is unloadable _index stays -1: count shows '0/5', Prev and Next are both disabled, and Ctrl+S says 'Open a workspace first.'
findings.observed: items ['a','x','b'], index 0; Next#1 → index 0, status 'Cannot open …/x.ima'; Next#2 → index 0, same status. GUI suite G3: unknown_ext.txt first item x.ima → index -1, next=False prev=False, count '0/5 · 0 done'; Prev from item 3 over noext_png stays at 3 twice.
findings.expected: Non-image files are excluded at build time (reported like missing paths), or navigation skips over an item that fails to load.

findings.title: A DICOM series directory listed in a list file is reported as 'listed path(s) not found' although it exists and the tree can load it
findings.description: build_workspace uses os.path.isfile, so a directory entry lands in ws.missing; the dock label then says 'N listed path(s) not found' and the tooltip shows a directory that plainly exists (the same directory loads fine when dragged from the tree, _make_series_meta returns a SeriesMeta). The README says 'one image path per line' but nothing tells the user that directories are unsupported or why the entry was rejected.
findings.observed: items ['a'], missing ['…/series'] with os.path.isdir → True and _make_series_meta(series) is not None. GUI: label '… 1 items, 0 done · 1 listed path(s) not found', tooltip = the mr20 directory.
findings.expected: Either the directory becomes an item (it is loadable) or the message distinguishes 'not a file / directories unsupported' from 'not found'.

findings.title: The same path listed twice becomes two separate jobs; Save & Next on the first re-presents the identical image as pending
findings.description: parse_list_file keeps duplicates and unique_stems only de-duplicates the stem ('a', 'a_1'; for entries outside the root all copies first get the full-path-mangled stem, then _1/_2). The user annotates the same image N times and the manifest gets N rows for one source. Lists assembled from spreadsheets or concatenated cohorts frequently contain repeats.
findings.observed: items [('a','a.dcm'), ('a_1','a.dcm')]. GUI suite G6 with lists/dup.txt (3 copies): 3 list rows, stems '…__imgs__a', '…__imgs__a_1', '…__imgs__a_2'; after Save&Next on #1, done=[True, False, False], index 1 shows the same file.
findings.expected: Identical normalised paths collapse to one item (or the user is told N duplicates were dropped).

findings.title: Unreadable list file (EACCES) is reported as 'No existing image paths found'
findings.description: parse_list_file swallows OSError and returns [] (workspace.py:116), so a list the user cannot read produces the same 'Empty list — No existing image paths found in …' warning as a list of missing paths. The user is sent to check the paths instead of the permissions.
findings.observed: dialogs: [('QMessageBox', 'Empty list', 'No existing image paths found in\n…/list.txt')] for a chmod-000 list containing one valid path.
findings.expected: A message naming the read error (permission denied).

findings.title: An image folder whose README.txt contains a bare file name is treated as 'images + list' and prompts for Workspace mode
findings.description: find_list_files calls every .txt/.lst/.csv/.tsv in the root a list as soon as one of its lines resolves to an existing file. A README.txt with a line 'LICENSE.txt' (any bare sibling file name) qualifies, so Open directory… on a plain image folder shows the 'Workspace mode' choice; picking List mode yields the non-image item 'LICENSE' ('Cannot open …/LICENSE.txt') and 'Image folder' as a missing path.
findings.observed: probe_workspace → (['…/a.dcm'], ['…/README.txt']); dialogs: [('QMessageBox', 'Workspace mode', 'readme holds 1 image files and 1 list file(s).\nWhich should define the job?')]. GUI suite G11: list mode → items ['LICENSE'], missing ['Image folder'], status 'Cannot open …/LICENSE.txt'. A README saying 'See LICENSE.txt for terms.' is correctly ignored.
findings.expected: Only files whose resolving entries are image files count as lists (or no prompt when the 'list' names no image).

findings.title: Open directory… stats every line of every .txt in the root: a 22 MB README.txt freezes the GUI thread for ~2.6 s
findings.description: find_list_files parses each top-level .txt/.lst/.csv/.tsv fully and calls os.path.isfile on every line until one exists; for a large prose file nothing exists, so all 400k lines are resolved and stat'ed synchronously inside the _open_dir slot with no progress indication or cancel. (A 10k-line list of missing paths takes 0.03 s; the cost scales with text size.)
findings.observed: probe_workspace on a folder with a.dcm + 22 MB / 400k-line README.txt: 2.59 s (find_list_files alone 2.58 s; GUI suite G10 Open directory… 2.83 s), result correctly image mode.
findings.expected: Sub-second open, e.g. by capping lines examined per candidate or skipping files above a size threshold.

reports.notes: Covered (pure-Python suite 59 checks, GUI suite 18 checks, 7 subprocess crash probes, 16 repro runs). PASS: CRLF .txt/.csv, CR-only .txt, trailing spaces/tabs (.txt) and trailing tab column (.tsv), quoted paths with commas (.csv) and "…"/'…' quotes (.txt), .tsv with header 'Path' and without header, header case 'ID,Path' / 'FILE,label', unknown header 'img_path,label' (dropped by heuristic → first column works), '# comment' lines before a header, short/ragged csv rows skipped, single-line list with and without EOL, header-only csv → [], empty and whitespace-only files → [], 5000-char path entry, '~' expansion (HOME patched), '..' entries resolving outside the list dir (all found, stems unique and free of os.sep), .lst with comment, .nii entry, UTF-8 accented filename, latin-1 file (replacement char, visibly reported missing), UTF-16 .txt (all missing, no exception), unterminated quote in csv, semicolon-delimited .csv (unsupported → 2 'missing' entries '…/1;/abs;x' → 'Empty list' warning, visible), tab-delimited .csv (→ 'a.dcm\tx' missing → 'Empty list'), id-first csv with unknown header 'subject_id,img_path,label' (→ ids as paths → 'Empty list'; matches README 'first column'), 10k-entry list (parse 0.03 s, build 0.11 s, 6667 items/3333 missing, stems unique, dock populate + first load 0.28 s), find_list_files on a 10k-missing list 0.03 s, root whose only list names missing files → 'Empty workspace' info, root with two lists → both found, README 'See LICENSE.txt for terms.' not a list, dock Open list… with all paths missing → 'Empty list' QMessageBox and no workspace, some missing → label '… N listed path(s) not found' with tooltip = missing paths joined by newline, 2MB random binary .txt is NOT safe (see ValueError crash). Also observed but not filed: 'id,label'-only csv yields a bogus '<listdir>/id' missing entry; header 'file.name,label' (dot in header) is counted as a missing path. BOM'd CSVs ('﻿path,label', '﻿id,path,label') parse correctly by luck of the unknown-header heuristic. All findings are in new files (workspace.py, annotation_dock.py) → preexisting=false. reports.lens: discovery — workspace.py item discovery (scan_images / is_image_path / probe_workspace / build_workspace / unique_stems / file_stem)

findings.title: unique_stems '_N' suffix collides with another file's natural stem -> two items share one stem
findings.description: The de-duplication loop at the end of unique_stems() appends '_<n>' to a repeated stem but never checks whether the generated name already belongs to (or will belong to) another path. Three files in ONE directory are enough: scan.nii, scan.nii.gz, scan_1.nii -> stems ['scan', 'scan_1', 'scan_1']. Pure API: unique_stems(['/r/k.png','/r/k.nii','/r/k_1.png'], '/r') == ['k','k_1','k_1']. Same with the '__' join path: a/b/x.png, a__b/x.png, a__b/x_1.png, q/x_1.png -> 'a__b__x_1' twice. Consequences observed: writing a manifest row for scan.nii.gz marks scan_1.nii done too (both key 'scan_1'); both items export to the identical <out>/png/scan_1_mask.png etc., so the second save silently overwrites the first. findings.title: PNG/JPEG export rounds while the canvas truncates: systematic +1 (inverted: -1) grey-level difference vs what is on screen
findings.description: window_to_uint8 computes (alpha*255 + 0.5).astype(uint8) but windowing.render_to_rgb (CPU and GPU path, unchanged by this feature) computes (alpha*255).astype(uint8). The docstring says 'the same way the canvas does' and README says 'what you see'. On a 0..4095 ramp with wc 2048/ww 4096, 124854/262144 px (47.6%) differ by exactly +1; with invert the saved value is 1 lower. Observed on real items through the dock: C.nii 105277/110592 px differ, CR x-ray (inverted) 1260742/3094616 px differ by -1, RGBA png 66532/74592 px. A constant image (ww=1 from percentiles) saves as 128 while the canvas shows 127; HU 40 at wc40/ww400 saves 128 vs canvas 127. Magnitude is only 1 LSB, but it is systematic and biases mean intensity by +0.48.
findings.observed: invert=False: 124854/262144 px differ, export-canvas in [0,1]; invert=True: differ in [-1,0]; constant image export=128 canvas=127
findings.expected: 0 px differ: saved 8-bit PNG/JPEG pixel-identical to canvas._rgb_buf[...,0] (same quantisation as render_to_rgb)

findings.title: Reloading an exported NIfTI in the viewer swaps pixel spacing (row/col); a second export swaps the file's zooms
findings.description: annotation_export._write_nifti writes affine diag(col_mm, row_mm, 1) so NIfTI zooms are (x=col, y=row) - correct NIfTI convention (reference suite asserts this). loader._run_nifti_load then reads px_row = zooms[0], px_col = zooms[1] even though it transposes data to (Z, Y, X) so rows are Y. For non-square spacing this is a swap: a DICOM with PixelSpacing (0.5, 0.25) exported and reloaded shows pixel_spacing (0.25, 0.5); re-exporting that panel writes zooms (0.5, 0.25) i.e. swapped vs the first file. Square-pixel fixtures (C.nii, CR, PNG) are unaffected. The broken line is in loader.py, which this feature does not modify, so it is a preexisting loader bug surfaced by the round trip (also affects any externally produced anisotropic NIfTI: MPR aspect ratio dz/dx uses the wrong value).
findings.observed: file zooms (0.25, 0.5, 1.0); reloaded in viewer pixel_spacing (row_mm, col_mm) = (0.25, 0.5), expected (0.5, 0.25); re-exported zooms (0.5, 0.25, 1.0) vs first export (0.25, 0.5, 1.0)
findings.expected: reloaded SeriesData.pixel_spacing == (0.5, 0.25) and zooms stable across save -> reload -> save

findings.title: Saving a 8192x8192 item blocks the GUI thread for ~19 s (all three formats) with no progress or busy indicator
findings.description: export_item runs synchronously inside the Save slot. Through the dock with a 8192x8192 PNG item, mask + rect + Original ticked: png 6.1 s, jpeg 1.3 s, nifti 11.7 s (415 MB written); pure-Python timings 6.9 / 1.7 / 22.0 s. The window cannot repaint or respond during this time and there is no status before the call returns. For the 2044x1514 CR fixture the same save takes 0.72 s, so this only matters for large rasters / high-res CR; worth a wait cursor or a status message at least.
findings.observed: png: dock._save returned after 6.1s; jpeg: 1.3s; nifti: 11.7s (GUI thread blocked, status label only updates afterwards)
findings.expected: Save either runs off the GUI thread or shows a busy cursor / progress while writing

findings.title: NIfTI mask of a 3-D NIfTI slice is saved with an identity-like affine: source orientation, translation and slice z are dropped, so it does not overlay the source in world space
findings.description: _write_nifti builds affine = diag(col_mm, row_mm, 1, 1) with origin (0,0,0) regardless of the source. For C.nii (axcodes LPS, non-diagonal affine, drawn on z=28) the saved mask has diag(1.1328, 1.1328, 1, 1) and origin 0: voxel (175,120) maps to world (198.2, 135.9, 0) in the mask but (33.4, -5.4, 6.7) in the source. Index-wise the mask IS aligned with source data[:, :, 28] (verified), so it is usable with manual slice selection, but loading mask + source in ITK-SNAP/3D Slicer will misplace it. README only promises 'pixel spacing in the affine', so this may be an accepted consequence of the 2-D limitation; flagging because the mask is otherwise index-aligned and the loss is silent.
findings.observed: saved mask affine diag [1.1328, 1.1328, 1, 1] origin [0,0,0]; source axcodes ('L','P','S'); same voxel world coords differ by >150 mm
findings.expected: mask affine = source affine with translation shifted to slice z (or a documented statement that the mask is index-aligned only)

findings.title: NaN pixels make window_to_uint8 emit numpy RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in cast' on stderr (NaN -> 0, inverted -> 255)

Float NIfTI parametric maps with NaN background are realistic input; the warning appears on stderr for every product (4 warnings per save). The CPU canvas path has the same cast and shows the same value, so the file still matches the screen.

findings.title: 1-widget-px drag in rect mode replaces the previous rectangle on a downscaled image
findings.description: _finish_rect guards against 'a click or a sliver' with `x1 - x0 < 2 or y1 - y0 < 2` in IMAGE pixels. The 2044x1514 CR image is displayed at 285x386 widget px in a quad cell (1 widget px = 5.3 image px), so a 1-px mouse jitter during a click yields a 6x6 image-px rect that silently replaces the user's rectangle; rectangles have no undo, so it must be redrawn.

findings.title: Brush cursor circle does not match the painted footprint on anisotropic reformats
findings.description: The cursor radius is `brush_r * r.width() / img_w` (x-scale only), while _paint_at stamps a disk of r image pixels in both axes. On the CORONAL reformat of C.nii (aspect 3.53) the cursor is an 8-px circle but each dab paints an 8.8 x 30.8 px ellipse on screen, so the user cannot see where the brush will land vertically. Mapping itself is correct (centroid == _image_coords in all orientations).

findings.expected: Cursor drawn as an ellipse with rx = r*sx, ry = r*sy (or the brush made circular on screen) so the preview matches the footprint

findings.title: Mask persists across slice scroll; Save pairs the displayed slice with a mask drawn on another slice, no slice index recorded
findings.description: set_image keeps the mask whenever the new slice has the same shape, so scrolling a 3-D volume carries the drawing silently onto every slice (and undo still undoes it there). Save then writes <stem>_image.nii.gz from the slice displayed at save time and <stem>_mask.nii.gz from the drawing made on a different slice, and manifest.csv has no slice column, so the pair is unrecoverably inconsistent. Adjacent to the documented 'annotations are 2-D on the displayed slice, one item per file' limitation; reported because the README wording implies the mask belongs to the slice it was drawn on, while nothing ties it to a slice or warns on scroll. Orchestrator should judge against the accepted-limitation list.
findings.observed: mask px on slice 40 after drawing on slice 10: 3323; saved image == slice 40: True, == slice 10: False; saved mask == slice-10 drawing: True; manifest columns: stem,source,saved_at,mask_pixels,x0,y0,x1,y1,formats,files

findings.title: Double-click in paint or rect mode toggles panel fullscreen
findings.description: The ViewCell eventFilter only exempts 'poly' from the double-click -> fullscreen toggle. Two quick brush dabs at the same spot (press/release/dblclick/release) paint once, push one undo entry and flip the panel to fullscreen (resizing the canvas under the cursor); a double-click in rect mode does the same. Recoverable by double-clicking again.

findings.title: Self-intersecting polygons are filled even-odd, leaving holes
findings.description: QPainter.drawPolygon uses Qt.OddEvenFill by default, so a pentagram outline fills the five points but leaves the central pentagon empty; a traced organ outline that accidentally crosses itself gets a hole in the crossed lobe. Bow-tie fills both lobes as expected. Design choice, but likely surprising for a segmentation brush; Qt.WindingFill would fill the interior.

findings.expected: Undo steps back through rectangle changes too (or at least Clear+Undo restores both), and Undo never discards a stroke the user did not intend to undo.

findings.title: Stale headers_ready/pixels_ready from a cancelled load land after load_meta(); Save in that window writes the PREVIOUS item's pixels under the CURRENT item's stem and marks it done
findings.description: LoaderWorker.request_load() cancels+joins the old thread but its already-emitted queued signals are still delivered afterwards, and ViewCell._on_headers_ready/_on_pixels_ready (view_cell.py:305/323) have no request-generation guard (pixels_ready only checks `self._sd is None`). So after Next, the cell can transiently hold sd = new item while canvas.displayed_pixels() still holds the old item's slice (set by the stale pixels_ready that arrived after load_meta's set_image(None)). AnnotationDock._save trusts `cell.series_data()` + `canvas.displayed_pixels()` to belong together: the path check passes (sd.meta.series_dir == item.path) and it exports the wrong pixels, writes the manifest row and marks the item done. Reproduced deterministically (repro_stale_loader_save.py: main thread blocked until A's thread finished, then load_meta(B)) AND with realistic ordering (t5_realistic_race.py: Next/Prev clicks posted through the event loop at random 1-30 ms gaps; 300 clicks -> stale sd seen at 12 clicks and an sd/pixels shape mismatch window twice; with --save, a Save inside that window wrote a 2044x1514 image as bpd1_20100102_1_image.png whose true shape is 2570x2040, status 'Saved 1 file(s)'). Final state after the loader settles is always consistent, so the only symptom is the wrong file on disk. The unguarded loader slots predate the feature, but the wrong export is new.

findings.title: Next gets stuck when the next item cannot be opened: _load_index returns before updating _index, so repeated Next/Save&Next never advances past the item
findings.description: If _make_series_meta(item.path) returns None (file vanished/moved after the workspace was opened, or no longer recognised), _load_index sets the status 'Cannot open ...' and returns without touching self._index or the list row. _step(+1) therefore recomputes the same index+1 every time: three Next clicks leave index=0 with Next still enabled. The user can only get past it by double-clicking a later item.

findings.expected: Next moves on to the following openable item (or at least to the unopenable item's row so another Next continues), e.g. select the row and keep stepping in the same direction.

findings.title: NIfTI items with anisotropic in-plane spacing export a swapped affine, and 2-D NIfTI items export with x/y axes swapped relative to the source
findings.description: loader._run_nifti_load sets sd.pixel_spacing = (zooms[0], zooms[1]) = (X mm, Y mm) (loader.py:375-377) while the displayed 3-D slice is (Y, X); the dock passes spacing=(pixel_spacing[0], pixel_spacing[1]) as (row_mm, col_mm) and _write_nifti builds affine diag(col_mm, row_mm) -> the exported file gets zooms (Y mm, X mm). For a 2-D NIfTI the loader shows the array untransposed (rows = X, 40x30 displayed as (40, 30)) while the exporter assumes rows = Y, so the written volume is (30, 40, 1): x' = source y, with the swapped zooms. Values and spacing are self-consistent inside the exported file but a mask exported from a 2-D NIfTI (or from an anisotropic 3-D one) no longer overlays the source volume in other tools. Invisible on C.nii (isotropic 1.1328 in-plane): there N3.5-N3.9 all pass. The loader convention is preexisting; the exporter's rows=Y assumption and the affine are new code.
